consumer: The frontend tile/sprite renderer drawing each monster, asking 'what threat color does the GUI paint this monster?' — a display tint, not a check anything evaluates.
scope: only the currently-visible monsters in the player's view, colored by the same threat-rating-to-color mapping the GUI applies
decisive_source: The decisive routine is NOT shown: the engine's monster threat-rating/color mapping (the function that turns a monster into its displayed threat tint, e.g. monster::color_with_outline / threat-rating coloring in the tilesheet/sidebar draw path) is absent; Excerpt 3 src/creature.cpp::Creature::sees only computes visibility (range/light/LOS), and Excerpts 1-2 only emit raw hp/scalar state via getters — none produce the displayed threat color.
divergence: A monster whose raw danger/difficulty would suggest one color but which the GUI tints differently due to display-only adjustment (e.g. a hallucination, or threat shading that lags or is dampened when the monster is only remembered/partly seen) — emitting the raw-state-derived color instead of the GUI's filtered display color exposes a wrong answer.
